newsitem.title: GERMANY: Leave Central African Republic, Bonn tells Germans.
newsitem.headline: Leave Central African Republic, Bonn tells Germans.

text.p: Germany advised its citizens in the Central African Republic to leave the country and said it was temporarily closing its embassy there due to clashes between peacekeepers and army mutineers which killed at least 80 people.
Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said a crisis on the scale of those in Rwanda, Congo and the Democratic Republic of Congo threatened to engulf the Central African Republic.
"The situation has already escalated so much that I have decided to temporarily close the German embassy in Bangui," Klaus Kinkel said in a statement.
"The situation in the heart of Africa must not become the African version of the domino theory," he said.
Fighting erupted in the Central African Republic last week between the disaffected soldiers and the peacekeepers, deployed to help restore peace after three army mutinies in under a year.
Witnesses said the two sides had clashed again on Thursday, exchanging automatic fire in Bangui.

Germany had urged its citizens to leave the country over the past year when trouble previously flared but subsequently advised them it was safe to return. The latest developments prompted Bonn to reissue its recommendation to leave.

"The Foreign Ministry once again urgently calls on all Germans in the Central African Republic to leave the country without delay. We warn against journeys to the Central African Republic," the ministry said in a statement.
A ministry spokesman said the Bagui embassy was small, with five staff. Germany's embassies in Sierra Leone, Liberia and Congo were also closed at the moment, he said.
Kinkel said the international community had to show a stronger commitment in its African policies to establish the foundations for peace, stability and economic development.
He said the world's leading industrialised nations and Russia had made clear at their summit in Denver last week that it was time Africa made a break from its troubled past.
"We must all help so that the vicious circle of the old mistakes is broken once and for all," he said.
